A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SpatiO study. All 36 pages of v1 and 42 pages of v3, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. Relocated analyses and prompts can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, component and routing ablations, cross-benchmark transfer experiments, and latency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those experimental results and adds MindCube evaluation, component-removal experiments, and hyperparameter, prompt, and agent-pool analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed agent pool, three roles, routing, reward updates, Bayesian estimation, dual EMA, and final reasoner remain unchanged. v1 Section 5.1 already specifies separate 150-sample calibration and a fixed inference configuration; v3's clarification and additional similarity-computation details do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds MindCube as a further zero-shot visual-domain generalization test (Appendix C.2, Table A8). All five previously evaluated benchmarks remain, including MMSI-Bench, whose results are relocated rather than newly introduced.

E2.justification: Table A2 adds explicit uniform-weight and majority-voting comparators; Table A5 adds fixed and random role-assignment comparisons. Existing named VLM, LoRA, and SpatialMAS comparators remain. Table A10's MATE/MoA/MoSA/VADAR comparison is conceptual, not an added numerical evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the stated CV-Bench/3DSRBench evaluation from 1,000-example samples to full datasets, although v1 already includes full-dataset tables and the retained numerical entries do not change. New experiments vary specialist count, beta, role assignment, prompt source, and pool composition. These substantially expand the reported evaluation design without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Tables A2, A5, and A6 test individual component removal, routing hyperparameters, fixed/random role assignments, LLM-generated prompts, and replacement of specialist agents. These substantially broaden the checks on component necessity and design sensitivity. Earlier cumulative ablations, confidence trajectories, transfer tests, and head-agent analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 specifies that the random agent-replacement results in Table A6 are averaged over three runs; v1 reports no corresponding repeated-run information. This is limited new reporting, without added seed specifications, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All ten original result tables retain their numerical entries after matching relocations. Substantial additions include component-removal results, sensitivity and pool/prompt variants, and MindCube accuracy of 44.39% versus Sa2VA's 42.72%. New prose also reports 84.7% accuracy and 19.8-second latency for SpatiO, but the cited Table A9 does not contain that comparison.

T1.justification: v1 uses an unspecified similarity operator in its reward; v3 formally defines it as rescaled cosine similarity between sentence embeddings (Equation 5). This is a limited addition to the mathematical specification. The routing, reward, Bayesian, and EMA relations otherwise remain equivalent, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: heterogeneous spatial specialists, reliability-based orchestration without model updates, and improved benchmark performance. Replacing 'optimization mechanism' with 'calibration mechanism' in the abstract clarifies terminology without changing those main claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion separating supervised calibration from unsupervised adaptation, explaining applicability when labeled calibration data are available, addressing benchmark leakage, and interpreting component and pool sensitivity. It also introduces an efficiency explanation based on selective specialist activation. The original limitations section remains largely unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds project-page access information, specifies sentence-embedding similarity and canonical option-text normalization, and documents the calibration/inference distinction more explicitly. Existing model identities, full prompts, decoding settings, and calibration hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references and discussion concerning RegionVLM, inherited truthful attention heads, and MindCube. Appendix C.4 adds a property-level comparison with existing multi-agent frameworks and positions novelty more explicitly as combining established capabilities rather than introducing a new algorithmic primitive.

P1.justification: Section 6 becomes a condensed summary, with its detailed analyses moved into Appendix C.1; detailed unseen-benchmark discussion moves into C.2. References move before the supplement, and new appendix subsections reorganize calibration, sensitivity, latency, and positioning discussions. This substantially changes document structure despite retaining much original prose.

P2.justification: v3 adds a notation table and Tables A2, A5, A6, A8, and A10, relocates several main-text displays into the appendix, and duplicates the existing latency breakdown as Table A9. Figure 2 is rendered at higher resolution, while the other original figure content and prompt displays are retained.

improvement.justification: The added ablations, sensitivity tests, and MindCube results strengthen empirical coverage, while clearer calibration documentation improves transparency. However, the new accuracy–latency claim cites Table A9, which only repeats the old module breakdown, and Table A5 marks beta=0.7 as default while Section 5.1 retains beta=5. These reporting inconsistencies weaken the added support, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
